thread.title: Alphabet Earnings Miss Views, Traffic Costs Soar, Shares Fall

author: REINHARDT KRAUSE
title: Alphabet Earnings Miss Views, Traffic Costs Soar, Shares Fall
text:
Google-parent Alphabet ( GOOGL ) reported fourth-quarter earnings Thursday that, excluding the impact of new corporate taxes, missed views as traffic acquisition costs, or TAC, soared.
X Google's TAC has been climbing, impacting gross margins. TAC is what Google pays partner websites to carry ads. During the quarter, TAC soared 33% to $6.45 billion from $4.85 billion a year earlier. TAC accounted for 24% of advertising revenue, up from 22% a year earlier.
Google's rising TAC has been linked to a contract renewal with Apple ( AAPL ) as well as internet searches shifting to mobile phones.
Fourth-quarter earnings were $9.70 a share, up 28% from a year earlier, missing views. Revenue rose 24% to $32.32 billion, topping consensus estimates. A year earlier, Alphabet earned $7.56 a share on sales of $26.06 billion. Analysts expected Alphabet to report earnings of $10.03 a share on sales of $31.85 billion for the period ended Dec. 31.
Advertising revenue rose 21.5% to $27.23 billion.
Shares in the internet search giant were down 3% to 1,146 in after-hours trading on the stock market today . Shares fell as much as 5% at one point.
Including the impact of corporate tax reform, Alphabet said it lost $4.35 per share in the quarter. The tax act resulted in additional tax expense of $9.9 billion in the quarter, Google said.
